Bug 1956768 - wasm: Do a CanGC string allocation for js-string/fromCharCodeArray. r=yury

Differential Revision: https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D244088
pr_title: Bug 1956768 - wasm: Do a CanGC string allocation for js-string/fromCharCodeArray. r=yury

files.diff:
diff --git a/js/src/jit-test/tests/wasm/regress/bug1956768.js b/js/src/jit-test/tests/wasm/regress/bug1956768.js
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..caeceb54256f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/js/src/jit-test/tests/wasm/regress/bug1956768.js
@@ -0,0 +1,22 @@
+let testModule = `(module
+(type $arrayMutI16 (array (mut i16)))
+
+(func $fromCharCodeArray
+    (import "wasm:js-string" "fromCharCodeArray")
+    (param (ref null $arrayMutI16) i32 i32)
+    (result (ref extern)))
+
+(func (export "test") (result externref)
+  (array.new_fixed $arrayMutI16 4 (i32.const 0) (i32.const 1) (i32.const 2) (i32.const 3))
+  i32.const 0
+  i32.const 4
+  call $fromCharCodeArray
+)
+)`;
+let module = new WebAssembly.Module(wasmTextToBinary(testModule), {builtins: ['js-string']});
+let instance = new WebAssembly.Instance(module, {});
+
+oomTest(() => {
+    let result = instance.exports.test();
+    assertEq(result, "\x00\x01\x02\x03");
+});

fix_commit.message: Bug 1992130 - Fix arguments types for std::copy. r=rhunt
fix_commit.author: Yury Delendik

findings.title: Heap buffer overflow from mismatched std::copy iterator types in StableWasmArrayObjectElements
findings.message: In StableWasmArrayObjectElements::StableWasmArrayObjectElements(), when a WasmArrayObject stores its data inline, the code copies the inline array data into a heap Vector sized to hold exactly numElements_ elements of type T. The call `std::copy(array->inlineStorage(), array->inlineStorage() + array->numElements_ * sizeof(T), ownElements_->begin())` passes a byte-typed (uint8_t*) source range whose length is expressed in bytes (numElements_ * sizeof(T)) but a T-typed destination iterator. std::copy advances the source and destination iterators in lockstep and performs exactly (last - first) iterations — here that is numElements_ * sizeof(T) iterations, each writing one element to the destination. Because the destination iterator is T* (not uint8_t*), each iteration advances the destination pointer by sizeof(T) bytes, so the loop writes sizeof(T) times more T-sized slots than the vector actually holds (which was resized to only numElements_ elements). This causes an out-of-bounds write past the end of the destination Vector's storage whenever sizeof(T) > 1, i.e. for every element type wider than a single byte. Additionally, the source pointer `array->inlineStorage()` points to the start of the inline storage region (which includes the DataHeader), not to `offsetOfInlineArrayData()` where the actual array element data begins, so even the bytes read are from the wrong offset. The overall effect is a heap-based buffer overflow write (and incorrect data source) reachable from WebAssembly GC array operations that use StableWasmArrayObjectElements, matching the reported 'incorrect boundary conditions' WebAssembly memory-safety vulnerability.
findings.suggestion: Use a source iterator with element type T that points at the correct array-data offset (offsetOfInlineArrayData(), not offsetOfInlineStorage()) and express the copy length in elements, not bytes, so that std::copy's source and destination iterators have matching, consistently-typed strides. Add a helper such as `T* inlineArrayElements()` that returns `offsetToPointer<T>(offsetOfInlineArrayData())`, then call `std::copy(src, src + array->numElements_, ownElements_->begin())`.
findings.suggestion_code:
const T* src = array->inlineArrayElements<T>();
std::copy(src, src + array->numElements_, ownElements_->begin());

ground_truth.root_cause: Type confusion between a byte-granularity source iterator (uint8_t*) with a byte-count length and an element-granularity destination iterator (T*) passed to std::copy, causing the loop trip count (computed as last-first in the source's element type) to be interpreted as T-sized elements against the destination, over-writing the destination buffer by sizeof(T)x.

must_cover.reason: Primary location of finding: Heap buffer overflow from mismatched std::copy iterator types in StableWasmArrayObjectElements
